repo_prior_art.cite: stat_transported_late_strength_frontier — a finite-cell transported-IV confidence-set frontier, not continuous polynomial-boundary transported-mean minimax risk.

published_prior_art.cite: KhanTamer2010 gives tail-dependent irregular inverse-weight rates and ZhangLiuWangTeng2025 treats covariate-shift moments; neither gives this two-sample causal Hölder boundary modulus.

BurmanGamaloGhosalKundu2026 proves bounded-overlap RiCOT for a distinct target-outcome experiment, while OriharaKomukaiLi2026 studies observational ATE extrapolation rather than this two-sample boundary-spliced estimator.

repo_prior_art.cite: stat_transported_late_strength_frontier concerns transported weak-IV strength, not a Hölder polynomial-source-boundary phase diagram.

published_prior_art.cite: No verified cited result gives the two-sample frontier with the a=1 logarithm, matching converse, and covariate-only target experiment.

ArmstrongKolesar2020 supplies bias-aware local-polynomial intervals and MaWang2020 supplies weak-overlap IPW inference, but neither treats learned calibrated transport weights plus an independent target empirical process.
CaiLow2004 supplies ordered-modulus adaptive-interval theory, but not this transported functional under polynomial source depletion.
Bull2012 concerns self-similar adaptive function bands in regular models, not joint overlap-and-smoothness adaptation for this two-sample transported functional.

soundness_flags.label: def:model-class; thm:minimax-lower; thm:sharp-frontier
soundness_flags.one_line: The stated domains allow c_->1 or c_+<1 (and, for the source density, c_+<a+1), making the bounded-factor density class empty; impose normalization-compatible constants or quantify the theorems only over a nonempty class.

soundness_flags.label: ass:source-sampling; ass:target-sampling; ass:sample-independence
soundness_flags.one_line: These three member assumptions are already entailed by def:model-class, which defines every experiment as P_S^{⊗n}⊗P_T^{⊗m}; retain the product experiment in one place only.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:sharp-frontier
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The frontier is conditional on the one-dimensional factorized polynomial-boundary class, bounded outcomes, known randomized propensity, and fixed regularity indices.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The sharp rate is only for this stated covariate-only transport model, not multivariate boundary geometry or observational treatment assignment.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: thm:fixed-class-honesty; oeq:self-similar-adaptation
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Honesty prespecifies (a,s,t,M), while joint adaptation is confined to the explicit self-similar subclass and remains open.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The accepted inference scope is fixed-class honesty; no unrestricted adaptive interval is claimed.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The target sample contains treated outcomes; Proposition 2.1 identifies τ_Q=E_Q[Y^Q]-E_Q[μ_0(X^Q)], Theorem 3.1 gives its two-sample efficient influence function, Assumption 1(iv) requires bounded density ratio, and later theorems give calibrated-weight convergence and efficient inference.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 1–6, Theorem 1 on p. 4, Appendix A.1 on pp. 12–17
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper studies q-th moments of an unknown function under covariate shift, proves a minimax lower bound in Theorem 1, and separately discusses unknown likelihood ratios and unlabeled target samples.

The article links inverse weights that must become arbitrarily large for point identification to tail-dependent slower-than-parametric estimation, including an exogenous-selection treatment-effect example.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 2, 13–16, and 20–21; local-polynomial bias correction and robust inference sections
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper analyzes weak-overlap IPW regimes, uses local-polynomial regression to correct trimming bias, and combines that correction with subsampling-based inference.
The paper develops honest scalar nonparametric-regression intervals based on local-polynomial or kernel estimators and bias-aware critical values.

source_verification_receipts.version: Author-accessible version of Annals of Statistics 32(5) article
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article gives adaptive confidence-interval lower bounds through between-class moduli and constructions through ordered moduli for linear functionals.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:1110.4985, published in Electronic Journal of Statistics 6
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper proves self-similarity conditions for honest adaptive confidence bands over Hölder classes in density, regression, and white-noise models.
The paper studies observational ATE estimation under limited propensity overlap through polynomial approximation and extrapolation of weighted estimands, not trial-to-target covariate-only transport.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Constrain c_- and c_+ so both normalized factors can be densities for every claimed a, or define a nonempty interior reference subclass and quantify all minimax claims over it.
Remove the duplicated sampling assumptions from the model-class membership list, leaving the product experiment as the sole sampling specification.
Promote the a=1 multiscale mixture to a separately stated construction lemma with explicit scale weights, total divergence bound, and accumulated separation.

recommended_next_step: Revise the nonemptiness and duplicated-assumption defects, then advance this genuine field-tier frontier to Stage 0.
